    proj := identity?  (desc becomes `∃! u, 𝟙 ≫ u = h`.) -/
noncomputable def symPowDataFake (C : K) (n : ℕ) : SymPowData C n where
  carrier := ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)
  proj := 𝟙 _
  desc := fun {T} h _ => ⟨h, Category.id_comp h, fun u hu => by
    simpa using hu⟩

    That would need `permAut C σ = 𝟙`. -/
example (C : K) (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    permAut C σ ≫ (symPowDataFake C n).proj = (symPowDataFake C n).proj := by
  show permAut C σ ≫ 𝟙 _ = 𝟙 _
  sorry

/-! PROBE 3: n = 1 — does `hproj` hold for `symPowDataOne`? -/
example (C : K) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 1)) :
    permAut C σ ≫ (symPowDataOne C).proj = (symPowDataOne C).proj := by
  show permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0 = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin 1 => C) 0
  rw [permAut_π]
  congr 1
  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

section
variable [BraidedCategory K] {C J A : K} {g : ℕ}

    [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
    (D : SymPowData C g) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)

    (φ : C ⟶ A) (ψ : J ⟶ A) (hφ : φ = aj ≫ ψ) :
    D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ := by
  classical
  refine (D.hom_ext_of_proj hproj ?_).symm

end

section PermAut

variable [HasFiniteProducts K]

/-- **The factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`.** For `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`,
the morphism `C^n ⟶ C^n` whose `i`-th component is the `σ i`-th projection; on
points, `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ (P_{σ 1}, …, P_{σ n})`. -/
noncomputable def permAut (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
  Pi.lift (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i))

omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
theorem permAut_π (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) :
    permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) := by
  simp only [permAut, Pi.lift_π]

end PermAut

section PowSum

variable [HasFiniteProducts K] [BraidedCategory K]

/-- **The `n`-fold sum morphism `C^n ⟶ A`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative
group object, the morphism sending `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, formed as
the product in the commutative monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` of the projections composed
with `φ`.

In the Albanese application `A` is an abelian variety and the group law is
written additively: this is `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`. -/
noncomputable def powSum {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ A :=
  ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)

/-- **Milne's "clearly this is symmetric".** The `n`-fold sum is invariant under
permuting the factors of `C^n`. The proof is exactly the commutativity of the
group law of `A`: in the *commutative* monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` a finite product is
invariant under reindexing (`Equiv.prod_comp`).

This is the hypothesis consumed by the universal property of the symmetric power
`Sym^n C`, which is what licenses the factorisation `C^n ⟶ Sym^n C ⟶ A`. -/
theorem powSum_perm {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ := by
  classical
  calc permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ
      = ∏ i, (permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
        map_prod (preHom (permAut C σ)) _ Finset.univ
    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) ≫ φ) :=
        Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [← Category.assoc, permAut_π]
    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
        Equiv.prod_comp σ (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)

/-- `powSum` is natural in the source: precomposition distributes over the sum. -/
theorem comp_powSum {C A W : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
    (u : W ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C))) :
    u ≫ powSum n φ = ∏ i, (u ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) := by
  classical
  exact map_prod (preHom u) _ Finset.univ

end PowSum

end CategoryTheory.MonObj

simp [Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, PartialMap.restrict]

/-- **Descent from a dense open into an abelian variety.**

Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, let `A`
be an abelian variety over `k̄`, let `V ⊆ X` be a **dense open**, and let
`h : V ⟶ A` be *any* morphism whose associated partial map is compatible with the
structure morphisms over `k̄`. Then there is a **unique** morphism `g : X ⟶ A`
restricting to `h` on `V`:

`∃! g : X ⟶ A, V.ι ≫ g = h`.

Existence is Milne Theorem 3.2 (`extend_to_av`), whose indeterminacy-locus input
— Milne Lemma 3.3 — is proved in `Albanese/Milne33.lean`, so this is
unconditional. Uniqueness is the agreement principle: two morphisms to a
separated scheme agreeing on a dense open of a reduced scheme are equal.

This is the extension half of `lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`. Note what
it does *not* require: no birationality, no properness of `V`, and nothing about
where `h` came from. Consequently the remaining gap in the Albanese descent is
purely the construction of the dense open and the morphism on it (i.e. inverting
`f^{(g)}` where it is an isomorphism), not the extension. -/
theorem exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open
    {X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [Smooth X.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [IsIntegral X.left] [IsReduced X.left]
    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    (V : X.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X.left)) (h : (V : Scheme) ⟶ A.left)
    (hover : (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
      = X.hom.toRationalMap) :
    ∃! g : X.left ⟶ A.left, V.ι ≫ g = h := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg, huniq⟩ := extend_to_av (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap hover
  exact ⟨g, (hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff V hV h g).mp hg,
    fun g' hg' => huniq g' ((hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff V hV h g').mpr hg')⟩

end Scheme.RationalMap

end AlgebraicGeometry

set_option autoImplicit false

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj

  [BraidedCategory K] {C J A : K}

-- (i) At g = 1 the forward direction needs NO homomorphy: pure associativity.
theorem forward_g1_no_monhom [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
    (D : SymPowData C 1) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 1), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
    (aj : C ⟶ J) (hf : D.proj ≫ f = powSum 1 aj)
    (φ : C ⟶ A) (ψ : J ⟶ A) (hφ : φ = aj ≫ ψ) :
    D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ := by
  classical
  refine (D.hom_ext_of_proj hproj ?_).symm
  rw [D.proj_comp_symAVMap, ← Category.assoc, hf]
  simp [powSum, hφ]

-- (ii) At g = 0 the forward direction FORCES pointedness of psi, so it is not
--      provable without a hypothesis on psi.
theorem forward_g0_forces_pointed [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] [MonObj J] [IsCommMonObj J]
    (D : SymPowData C 0) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 0), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
    (aj : C ⟶ J) (hf : D.proj ≫ f = powSum 0 aj)
    (φ : C ⟶ A) (ψ : J ⟶ A) (hφ : φ = aj ≫ ψ)
    (H : D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
    D.proj ≫ f ≫ ψ = D.proj ≫ f ≫ ψ := rfl

-- (iii) hproj holds for the FAKE datum at n = 0 and n = 1 (permAut is the identity).
example (C : K) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 1)) :
    permAut C σ = 𝟙 (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin 1 => C)) := by
  apply Pi.hom_ext; intro b
  rw [permAut_π, Category.id_comp]
  congr 1; exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

end ReviewProbe3

simp [Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, PartialMap.restrict]

/-- **Descent from a dense open into an abelian variety.**

Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, let `A`
be an abelian variety over `k̄`, let `V ⊆ X` be a **dense open**, and let
`h : V ⟶ A` be *any* morphism whose associated partial map is compatible with the
structure morphisms over `k̄`. Then there is a **unique** morphism `g : X ⟶ A`
restricting to `h` on `V`:

`∃! g : X ⟶ A, V.ι ≫ g = h`.

Existence is Milne Theorem 3.2 (`extend_to_av`), whose indeterminacy-locus input
— Milne Lemma 3.3 — is proved in `Albanese/Milne33.lean`, so this is
unconditional. Uniqueness is the agreement principle: two morphisms to a
separated scheme agreeing on a dense open of a reduced scheme are equal.

This is the extension half of `lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`. Note what
it does *not* require: no birationality, no properness of `V`, and nothing about
where `h` came from. Consequently the remaining gap in the Albanese descent is
purely the construction of the dense open and the morphism on it (i.e. inverting
`f^{(g)}` where it is an isomorphism), not the extension. -/
theorem exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open
    {X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [Smooth X.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [IsIntegral X.left] [IsReduced X.left]
    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    (V : X.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X.left)) (h : (V : Scheme) ⟶ A.left)
    (hover : (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
      = X.hom.toRationalMap) :
    ∃! g : X.left ⟶ A.left, V.ι ≫ g = h := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg, huniq⟩ := extend_to_av (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap hover
  exact ⟨g, (hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff V hV h g).mp hg,
    fun g' hg' => huniq g' ((hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff V hV h g').mpr hg')⟩

end Scheme.RationalMap

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- **Descent from a dense open into an abelian variety.**

Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, let `A`
be an abelian variety over `k̄`, let `V ⊆ X` be a **dense open**, and let
`h : V ⟶ A` be *any* morphism whose associated partial map is compatible with the
structure morphisms over `k̄`. Then there is a **unique** morphism `g : X ⟶ A`
restricting to `h` on `V`:

`∃! g : X ⟶ A, V.ι ≫ g = h`.

Existence is Milne Theorem 3.2 (`extend_to_av`), whose indeterminacy-locus input
— Milne Lemma 3.3 — is proved in `Albanese/Milne33.lean`, so this is
unconditional. Uniqueness is the agreement principle: two morphisms to a
separated scheme agreeing on a dense open of a reduced scheme are equal.

This is the extension half of `lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`. Note what
it does *not* require: no birationality, no properness of `V`, and nothing about
where `h` came from. Consequently the remaining gap in the Albanese descent is
purely the construction of the dense open and the morphism on it (i.e. inverting
`f^{(g)}` where it is an isomorphism), not the extension. -/

    {X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [Smooth X.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [IsIntegral X.left] [IsReduced X.left]
    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    (V : X.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X.left)) (h : (V : Scheme) ⟶ A.left)
    (hover : (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom

  exact ⟨g, (hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff V hV h g).mp hg,

The pattern being defended: replace a sorry-BODIED definition (here Pic0.SymmetricPower) with a STRUCTURE carrying its universal property, and prove the downstream argument over the structure. It is the right move, and this lane executed it correctly. But the usual defence -- "the structure is inhabited, so nothing is vacuous" -- is the weakest of the three checks and on its own proves very little.

CHECK 1 (weak, usually passes trivially): is the structure inhabited? A universal-property structure whose only field is "every map factors uniquely through proj" is ALWAYS inhabited by carrier := source, proj := identity, desc := <h, id_comp, ...>. Costs three lines. Do not quote it as non-vacuity.

CHECK 2 (the real one): is the structure PLUS the side hypotheses the downstream theorems actually take jointly inhabited? Here the theorems all also take hproj (symmetry of proj), which the identity datum fails for n >= 2. That pair is what needs a witness, and it is what the docstring should claim.

CHECK 3 (the one nobody runs): at the exhibited inhabitant, is the advertised hard step still non-trivial? Here the only symmetric inhabitant is n = 1, and the homomorphy step advertised as "Milne step 5" is provable WITHOUT the IsMonHom hypothesis at n = 1 (a 1-fold product is one factor). So the exhibited instance does not exercise the claimed content.

TWO METHODS WORTH KEEPING, both cheap and both used here:
* Load-bearingness by deletion. lean_minimal_hypotheses on the headline; then, for a specific suspected-decorative binder, delete it by hand and re-run the SAME proof -- the residual goal names exactly what the binder buys. That is how "IsMonHom is load-bearing" was confirmed rather than assumed (residual goal: powSum g aj >> psi = powSum g phi).
* Axiom attribution by a generic twin. State the same theorem with the sorry-carrying object replaced by an arbitrary object of the same type, and print axioms on both. Clean twin + dirty original attributes the sorryAx to the substituted object -- PROVIDED you diff the two binder lists and confirm nothing else weakened. Here the diff is exactly (jacobianScheme C, with its four instances derived) vs (J, with the four instances assumed), no hypothesis dropped; attribution holds.' 2>&1 | tail -2
